package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate JavaScript libraries but contain obfuscated or plaintext code that, upon installation, collects and exfiltrates sensitive files (Kubernetes config, SSH keys, system fingerprinting data) to an external server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. The behavior is covert, deceptive, and not expected from legitimate packages.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads sensitive files (SSH private key, Kubernetes config) and system information, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects highly sensitive files and system information and sends them to an external server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not access or exfiltrate SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, or fingerprinting data during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System diagnostic tools or backup utilities may access such files, but only with explicit user consent and never during package installation.
key_indicators: Use of os and fs modules to gather user and system data
Network request to hardcoded external domain (app.threatest.com)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
var _0xabc=['os','fs','readFileSync','homedir','id_rsa','kube','config','hostname','userInfo','username','https','request','app.threatest.com','/api/v1/collect','Content-Type','application/json'];
// ...obfuscated code that decodes and executes similar logic as snippet_1
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated version of snippet_1: collects SSH keys, Kubernetes config, and system info, then exfiltrates to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent, but the decoded logic matches the plaintext version that exfiltrates sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Obfuscated code in postinstall scripts is highly unusual for legitimate packages, especially when it accesses sensitive files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection, but not for scripts that run automatically and access user secrets.
key_indicators: Same file access and network exfiltration as plaintext version

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., @am-fe/hooks, @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable).

attack_chain.leads_to: Script collects sensitive files and system information.

attack_chain.action: Script reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.kube/config, and gathers system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, home directory).
Script sends collected data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data; compromise complete.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Network requests to hardcoded external domains during installation
Obfuscated JavaScript code in install scripts
Collection of system fingerprinting data (username, hostname) during install
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with obfuscated or plaintext exfiltration logic
Presence of postinstall field in package.json referencing suspicious scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com
Connections to 172.67.141.49 or 104.21.9.30 during npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files (e.g., SSH keys, Kubernetes configs) and make outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Flag packages with obfuscated install scripts or those referencing suspicious external endpoints. Use endpoint monitoring to detect unexpected file access and exfiltration attempts during package installation.
